task_description: Implement all four feature groups on the laya-browser-mcp Autopilot/overlay stack, additively and backward-compatibly: A) Reliability & self-healing (auto-retry with self-healing refs, post-action settle detection, loop-detection/stuck guard); B) Trust & safety (secret redaction, human-in-the-loop confirmation via MCP elicitation, opt-in destructive guard for Assist tools); C) Perception cost & speed (accessibility-tree snapshot backend + benchmark, snapshot diffing with delta escalation, viewport-priority capture); D) Observability (session trace/replay export tool, structured MCP progress notifications). All new config via typed LAYA_-prefixed knobs parsed once in src/config.ts; README updated; real headless tests added for each feature; no networkidle/slowMo; stderr-only; no secrets in logs.

verification.summary: npm run typecheck clean; npm run build clean; npm run test = 208 passed / 3 skipped (the 3 pre-existing skips - WebKit launch smoke + two real-weights Autopilot tests - preserved; baseline was 154/3, +54 new tests incl. review-fix regression tests). npm run bench produced the C1 comparison: domwalk 902 ms/case vs aria 1013 ms/case, both 4/4 success / 100% ops-coverage. No Dockerfile in repo so docker_build skipped. Test quality reviewed: new tests (redaction-loop, progress-notifications, autopilot-reliability A1/A2/A3, export-run) drive the real Autopilot loop against real headless chromium and assert against the real DOM (e.g. inputValue() confirms the real secret is typed while the transcript is masked), contrast feature-on vs feature-off behaviour (loopDetection stuck vs max_steps), and parse the actual written replay artifacts; they would fail if the implementation were reverted.
